claims.claim: Anyone can order certified copies of civil registration certificates.
claims.quote: Anyone who can identify the entry in the register is entitled to apply for a copy certificate.
claims.note: Only a single council page says this, and it adds the condition that you must be able to identify the entry; the GRO pages do not say who can order.

claims.claim: Certificates are ordered from GRO for events registered in England and Wales.
claims.quote: You need to register on the General Register Office ( GRO ) website to get a copy of a birth, adoption, death, marriage or civil partnership certificate in England and Wales.
claims.note: GRO supplies copies of certificates for England and Wales.

claims.quote: Certificates cost £12.50 and are sent 4 days after you apply.

claims.claim: With a GRO index reference, certificates are sent 4 days after applying.
claims.quote: Certificates cost £12.50 and are sent 4 days after you apply.
claims.note: The 4-day timing is the standard case, contrasted with the slower one for orders without an index reference.

claims.claim: Without a GRO index reference, certificates are sent 15 working days after applying and cost £3.50 extra per search.
claims.quote: If you do not have a GRO index reference number , you’ll have to pay £3.50 extra for each search. Certificates are sent 15 working days after you apply.
claims.note: Both the search fee and the 15 working days match.

claims.quote: If you need the certificate sooner, you can use the priority service for £38.50.

claims.claim: Certificates can also be ordered from the local register office.
claims.quote: You can also order certificates from the local register office where the birth, death or marriage was registered.
claims.note: Local register offices are named as another place to order, specifically the office where the event was registered.
